checklist.name: low HDL cholesterol
quotes: characterized by an absence or extremely low level of high-density lipoprotein (HDL)-cholesterol (HDL-C)
Plasma HDL-C is mostly low, at 5 mg/dL or less
checklist.why: The defining lipid abnormality; levels also separate homozygotes from heterozygous relatives, whose decrease the review calls inconsistent.

checklist.name: low apolipoprotein A-I
quotes: the apoA-I concentration is 10 mg/dL or less
plasma HDL-C and apoA-I levels are often reduced to about 50% of that in normal subjects
checklist.why: Second required laboratory criterion; also reduced to varying degrees in heterozygotes.

checklist.name: orange-colored or enlarged tonsils
quotes: A typical finding of this disorder is orange-colored tonsils
The tonsils of patients are lobulated and swollen and present a bright orange or yellow-grey surface.
checklist.why: The typical physical finding and a diagnostic clinical symptom; the review calls tonsillar swelling specific to Tangier disease.

checklist.name: recurrent tonsillitis or tonsillectomy
quotes: A history of recurrent tonsillitis or tonsillectomy is often noted.
checklist.why: Often noted history; tells a reader whether tonsils could still be examined.

checklist.name: splenomegaly
quotes: splenomegaly and associated thrombocytopenia and/or reticulocyte hyperplasia may be present
checklist.why: Major physical finding and part of a diagnostic clinical symptom.

checklist.name: hepatomegaly
quotes: Hepatomegaly is also observed in about one-third of cases
checklist.why: Seen in about one third of cases; listed apart from splenomegaly because the review gives it separately.

checklist.name: thrombocytopenia
quotes: splenomegaly and associated thrombocytopenia
checklist.why: Hematologic consequence of splenomegaly named by the review.

checklist.name: reticulocytosis
quotes: thrombocytopenia and/or reticulocyte hyperplasia may be present
checklist.why: Second hematologic finding the review links to splenomegaly.

checklist.name: lymphadenopathy
quotes: major physical findings are orange-colored pharyngeal tonsils, hepatosplenomegaly, corneal opacity, lymphadenopathy, and peripheral neuropathy
cholesterol accumulation in other organs, such as lymph nodes, thymus, intestinal mucosa, and skin
checklist.why: Major physical finding in the abstract; lymph nodes are a site of cholesterol accumulation.

checklist.name: corneal opacity
quotes: Its accumulation in the cornea causes corneal opacity.
checklist.why: Major physical finding and diagnostic clinical symptom.

checklist.name: skin lipid deposits
quotes: cholesterol accumulation in other organs, such as lymph nodes, thymus, intestinal mucosa, and skin
checklist.why: Skin is named as a site of cholesterol accumulation.

checklist.name: intestinal mucosal lipid deposits
quotes: cholesterol accumulation in other organs, such as lymph nodes, thymus, intestinal mucosa, and skin
checklist.why: Intestinal mucosa is named as a site of cholesterol accumulation.

checklist.name: peripheral neuropathy
quotes: Various peripheral neuropathies, ranging from mild to severe, have been reported.

Peripheral neuropathy appears as a recurrent asymmetric disorder of peripheral nerves including cranial nerves, as neuropathy with symmetry in the lower limbs, or syringomyelia-like peripheral neuropathy
checklist.why: Major finding and diagnostic clinical symptom; the review calls it specific to Tangier disease among inherited low-HDL disorders.

checklist.name: reduced tendon reflexes
quotes: Reduced deep perception and tendon reflexes are rare.
checklist.why: Examination sign the review names (as rare); case reports routinely state reflexes.

checklist.name: reduced deep sensation
quotes: Reduced deep perception and tendon reflexes are rare.
checklist.why: Examination sign the review names (as rare).

checklist.name: coronary artery disease
quotes: premature coronary artery disease is frequently observed
diffuse calcified coronary artery lesions
checklist.why: Frequent and premature; the main clinical problem and part of the cardiovascular-disease criterion.

checklist.name: non-coronary atherosclerotic arterial disease (e.g. brachiocephalic or iliac stenosis)
quotes: Advanced systemic atherosclerotic lesions in male patient with Tangier disease in his 50s
C: brachiocephalic artery, D: left iliac artery, E: right external iliac artery
checklist.why: The review shows systemic atherosclerosis beyond the coronaries; kept apart from coronary disease so neither sits inside the other.

checklist.name: glucose intolerance or impaired insulin secretion
quotes: treatment for glucose intolerance might be required because impaired insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells has occasionally been reported
checklist.why: Metabolic finding the review names and links to atherosclerosis.

checklist.name: low LDL cholesterol
quotes: Plasma LDL-C is also reduced, to around 37% of the average normal level.
checklist.why: Characteristic lipid finding; notable because coronary disease occurs despite it.

checklist.name: hypertriglyceridemia
quotes: increased triglyceride in the plasma of Tangier patients
checklist.why: Plasma lipid abnormality the review names.

left_out: cardiovascular disease (broad criterion term): split into coronary and non-coronary atherosclerotic disease to avoid a broad item containing narrower ones
diffuse coronary artery calcification: a narrower form of coronary artery disease

cranial nerve involvement, symmetric lower-limb neuropathy, syringomyelia-like neuropathy, sensory/motor/mixed neuropathy: patterns of peripheral neuropathy, so they would sit inside it; helpers can note the pattern in free text
thymic lipid deposits: named as an accumulation site but rarely assessable in case reports
remnant lipoproteins or small dense LDL particles: specialised lipoprotein analyses seldom reported per patient
liver dysfunction: the review says it is not usually present
xanthomas: the review says they are found only in familial apoA-I deficiency, not Tangier disease
increased inflammatory cytokine secretion and accelerated apoA-I catabolism: mechanistic findings, not per-patient clinical findings
hypertension, smoking, diabetes mellitus: named only as atherosclerotic risk factors to manage, not as features of the disease
notes: The review is short (one Japanese consensus review). It yields about 18 clearly clinical features; to reach 20 I included low HDL-C and low apoA-I although they are required diagnostic criteria (rule 3 says to avoid results every patient has by definition). They are kept because the extraction will also cover heterozygous relatives, in whom the review says the decrease is variable, so the items are not uniformly 'observed'. A reviewer may prefer to swap them for remnant/small dense LDL or thymic deposits. 'Reduced tendon reflexes' and 'reduced deep sensation' are examination signs rather than neuropathy types, but a strict reader might see them as overlapping with peripheral neuropathy. 'Reticulocytosis' renders the review's 'reticulocyte hyperplasia'. 'Skin' and 'intestinal mucosal lipid deposits' rest on a single sentence listing accumulation sites.
